events.continuity_hook: The next session can narrow the outbound schedule once the audit host confirms Monday evening access and can settle the return after Friday's agenda is finalized.
events.interaction_goal: Compare practical Monday outbound flights and identify Friday return options that remain viable under both possible audit end times.
events.scenario_brief: Priya has a four-day supplier audit in Raleigh beginning Tuesday, April 16. She must travel from San Francisco and reach the site by 8:00 a.m. Tuesday, so she is considering Monday arrivals and needs a workable round-trip shortlist; the audit may finish either Friday afternoon or early evening.

events.continuity_hook: Flight timing is nearly settled, but the final choice depends on comparing total travel time and whether the later Friday departures still have acceptable connections.
events.interaction_goal: Recheck the shortlist against the confirmed schedule and select the most practical outbound and return itinerary.
events.scenario_brief: The Raleigh host has confirmed that Priya can enter the facility Monday evening, and the Friday closing meeting is now scheduled through 4:30 p.m. She wants to reduce the shortlist to an outbound that leaves enough time for check-in and a return that does not require leaving the site early.

events.continuity_hook: The air itinerary is settled; lodging remains the last administrative item before the trip can be submitted for approval.
events.interaction_goal: Compare a small set of compliant hotels and identify one with a manageable site commute and the required business-travel logistics.
events.scenario_brief: With the flights selected, Priya needs lodging for four nights near the audit site in Morrisville. The company rate cap applies, and she needs to verify commute time for an 8:00 a.m. start, late check-in after her Monday flight, and whether the property can provide an itemized business receipt.

events.continuity_hook: No dates or resort are selected yet; the next step will depend on which weekend offers a better combination of room availability and spa scheduling.
events.interaction_goal: Evaluate both weekend windows and produce a concise resort-and-date shortlist for the couple to discuss.
events.scenario_brief: Priya and her spouse are considering a three-night wellness trip to Sonoma in late May, using either Memorial Day weekend or the following weekend. They will drive from San Francisco, and they want to compare how the two date windows affect resort availability, spa appointment access, and overall cost before choosing dates.

events.continuity_hook: The travel dates are fixed, while the resort decision depends on confirming spa times and comparing the complete cost rather than the advertised nightly rate.
events.interaction_goal: Verify the unresolved spa and fee details, compare the two complete packages, and determine which resort better fits this trip.
events.scenario_brief: Priya and her spouse have chosen the weekend after Memorial Day and narrowed the trip to two Sonoma resorts. One has stronger spa availability but a higher room total; the other includes breakfast and parking, but its preferred treatment times are uncertain. They need a like-for-like comparison of the full stay and cancellation terms.

events.continuity_hook: The stay is booked; guest details and treatment timing must be corrected before the deadline to avoid arrival or spa check-in problems.
events.interaction_goal: Review the confirmation, identify the reservation details requiring correction, and prepare the exact administrative follow-up needed with the resort.
events.scenario_brief: The couple booked the resort with the stronger spa schedule, but the confirmation lists only one guest on the room and shows the massage appointments without the requested staggered start times. Priya wants the reservation details checked before the free-cancellation deadline and needs both guests reflected correctly.
